name: chat-first-json
description: Chat-first app with local JSON data: a chat on one side, a served pane on the other. Python (FastAPI) serves the pane and the chat API; data lives in JSON files; pytest for unit tests, Playwright for the served pane. No deployment.

stack._comment: Versions are security-relevant MINIMUMS, not exact pins - resolve and install the latest version satisfying each range when scaffolding.
stack._comment_backend: Empty on purpose and load-bearing for adopt matching: adopt scores a profile by the dependency names it declares here, so listing fastapi/uvicorn would pull every FastAPI repo away from the profile that fits it. See notes.

folder_structure.app/: FastAPI application (app/main.py serves the pane and the chat API)
folder_structure.app/static/: The served pane (HTML, CSS, vanilla JS) next to the chat
folder_structure.data/: Local JSON data files (the only storage; no external service)
folder_structure.e2e/: Playwright specs run against the served pane (*.spec.ts)

notes: Backend: FastAPI served by uvicorn (add both to pyproject.toml at their latest versions). They are not listed under stack.backend on purpose: adopt scores a profile by the dependency names it declares, and a FastAPI entry would pull every FastAPI repo away from the profile that fits it. A bundled profile's e2e layer always runs through playwright_runner.py (npx playwright test with the json reporter), so testing.e2e.command documents that rather than selecting it. A chat-first app has no separate deploy step (deploy_target none): there is no deploy block and no CI template mapping for this profile, deliberately. The dev_server block is a single executable command without shell metacharacters because the WebUI preview starts only that block and ignores 'services'. /api/health must answer 200 once the app is up: dev_server.py readiness (which Browser Verify starts) and the smoke test (--health-path) wait on it.
